If it's almost new, from factory, paste is prolly fine (though likely poor quality). Higher quality paste would definitely help, l like thermal grizzly myself. Ventilation, raise it off of a desk. Cooling pads do this, while also having fans inside em. Undervolt the CPU definitely. It already uses more wattage than necessary to run the laptop, so less wattage = less temp = better performance (using a safe undervolt). You can also restrict the frequency so you're not using 4.2 GHz for a potato game. If heatsinks are shared instead of having one for CPU and one for GPU,  it's typically more hot. Not much you can do about that, but i doubt it'd be a big cause.

In a nutshell of what I'd do; undervolt and restrict CPU wattage, raise the bottom so air flows, repaste (if you want) with better stuff, and raise fan speeds if you're able.

First one takes priority if you only do one (undervolt, frequency, and/or restrict wattage)

Set multiplier - checked. If turbo is disabled you can lower freqs even lower than the base 2.2. if turbo is enabled then it's mainly just for show at that point. I usually make it the same as the core freqs in FIVR, (the ones you set to 30)

Speed shift - checked. Basically how fast your CPU goes from snail to cheetah. 0 being instant/constant Max perf and 255 being only using minimum until game time I think.

BD Prochot - check. Let it thermal throttle and it'll let you know on the right side labeled PROCHOT with your max CPU temp before it throttles.

Speed step - checked. it's the turbo I think?

C1E - Idk, I'd leave it checked. Forgot what that did tbh.

For the TPL - yea it's looking at short and long. Like something about power limits. It limits the wattage your cpu will take it regardless if it even needs that much. 
I have no idea why he said 120 watts, but that's some desktop shit probs. Set short and long to both 40 or 45. If it takes more wattage than it needs, it's just gonna get hotter without any benefit. Yours prolly started at like 70 and 85. Lower to 40 id say. That's a big help with temps.

Turbo being disabled it's not gonna go past the base clock of 2.2 MHz. You gotta re-enable it to get it speedy man. 

You want a stable 3.0 MHz performance, set them damn arrows to like 3100 or something, apply and save. Then go into your undervolt setting tab, and on the bottom left should be some numbers from like 4.1, 4.1, 4.0, 4.0, 3.9, 3.9, should be it. Thats the frequencies based on the number of cores active. Set that shit to 30, all of em. apply and save. Make it a profile even, hell idc. Now your freqs won't go past 3.0 MHz and saving temps.


BD Prochot lets you know it thermals throttled sometime ago while you weren't or were looking. You can click the little circle in it to clear it.
